Diagrams.SequenceDiagram: Runner -> resolve report path -> reject repo-internal path before any mutation accepted path -> one Bun suite attempt -> current JUnit report -> current ranking child failure -> preserve exact child exit, retain report if produced missing/bad report after child success -> diagnostic nonzero, no ranking spawn failure -> diagnostic nonzero, no retry final full CI once -> apply/archive -> focused CloseEvidence + combined Git inventory

NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The declaration-count guard was never a coverage measure. It compared `it(`/`test(` occurrences in an existing file at HEAD against the same file at base `2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`. Applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/spec.xml:527-536`) installed it as a temporary test-deletion brake during a time-budget optimization, and its own text says so. It cannot see executed code, assertion strength, or coverage added in a new file, and it cannot see an assertion deleted from inside a surviving test — the Goodhart weakness. It also fails open: `coverageRegressions` (`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) runs `git show` (`:351`) and `continue`s on a non-zero exit (`:353-354`), so in a depth-one checkout it compares nothing and reports green. Reproduced 2026-09-30 UTC at base `06996d…` on a throwaway depth-one clone: `git cat-file -e 2434fd4…` exits 1 and `git show 2434fd4…:scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` exits 128, while the same `git show` exits 0 in the full repository. A green produced by a failed lookup is not evidence. The guard is retired because it measures the cheapest proxy of behavior rather than behavior, and it can be trivially green when the lookup it depends on never runs.
The `validate` job's `fetch-depth: 0` existed only to feed that guard's historical read. Applied `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-6-62765C22/spec.xml:712-720`) originally tied full history to a `6dd1d95` mint control; `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4` retired that control and recorded at `spec.xml:28-38,74-82` that the declaration-count guard is now the only reason for full history, naming this successor at `design-context.xml:183-187` as the bundle that retires the guard, the retitled depth assertion, and `fetch-depth: 0` together. Retiring one without the other is incoherent: the guard without the depth cannot read its base, and the depth without the guard reads nothing.
The replacement is not a new score. The discipline that continues is contract-specific: behavioral tests, real CLI happy and refusal paths, byte-preservation checks where promised, and targeted fault mutations that prove a test can fail. Static lint and typecheck remain structural checks, not coverage claims. Measured executed-code coverage is diagnostic only and is deferred to a future separately ratified change. This is the honest reading of the maintainer's decision to remove the guard and document why, rather than substitute another number that looks like coverage.
The committed timing artifact is deleted rather than repaired. It was introduced under `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/spec.xml:484-490`; its freshness predicate came from applied `C-CI-LINT-AND-PLAN-SHAPE-1-3526D6F0/spec.xml:358-372` and compared only the file list and the artifact's own count sum (`scripts/test-metrics.ts:82-98`), so a same-file test edit was invisible. Rather than add a digest, a schema version, a group field, a provisional artifact, and a no-write-when-fresh branch to a cache that exists only to avoid recomputing a JUnit report, this bundle removes the cache. `scripts/test-metrics.ts` becomes a one-suite wrapper: it spawns `bun test` exactly once, writes a brand-new raw JUnit report for that invocation to a unique directory under `os.tmpdir()` outside the repository (or to the documented `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` override), removes any pre-existing file at the resolved report path before the spawn, prints the report location, parses the current report for the slowest-test ranking, propagates the child's actual nonzero exit, and retains the failure report. A report generated afresh for every invocation is current by construction, so there is no freshness predicate to fail open and no committed churn to manage. An override that resolves inside the repository is refused before any filesystem mutation — `mkdir`, unlink, or spawn — and the check is canonical rather than a lexical prefix, so a symlinked parent or a `..` path cannot write a raw report into the tree. The runner also refuses rather than guessing: a successful child whose report is missing, unreadable, or malformed is a diagnostic nonzero with no ranking and no reuse of an earlier report; a spawn failure is a diagnostic nonzero with no retry; and a failing child's exact OS exit code survives bad report parsing, with any produced report bytes retained.
The kept surface is the parser, the ranking, and the one-suite runner. `parseJUnit` extracts file, name, and milliseconds from the current report; `rankSlowest` orders descending by milliseconds; the runner prints the ranking. The behavioral tests drive the real runner through the absolute Bun executable in a disposable project with a fake inner `bun` on `PATH`, so the inner spawn is intercepted but the outer process is genuinely the production entry. A passing run produces a current report and ranking; a failing run leaves the OS exit nonzero and retains the report; restoring the assertion passes again. The fake records its invocations, so one inner suite spawn per run is observed rather than asserted across a fake outer process. No test-only seam is mandated; a sensible implementation seam is permitted if the implementation needs one.
CI uploads the current report with `always()` so a failing suite still produces evidence. The `validate` job sets `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` to `${{ runner.temp }}/ngrace-test-reports/junit.xml`, outside the repository, and the upload step references the current verified `actions/upload-artifact` major. The upload step sets no `continue-on-error`, so a successful upload cannot change the job's failure outcome: the earlier failing step still fails the job. Only the current report is uploaded, and no unrelated temporary data is.
The retirement is honest about what it does **not** replace. No broad floor stands in for `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT`: the removed guard was a declaration-count proxy, never a suite-wide floor, and this bundle adds no percentage or test-volume score. The counterweights the retired bundle carried are retained: visibility into the current slow tests survives as the raw ranking, the single suite invocation survives as `validate:ci` through `test:metrics` once (checked by the retained `validateCiRerunsSuite` guard), committed timing noise is removed by deleting the artifact, and unrelated behavior is preserved because every other guard and assertion stays. A passing `bun test` is not claimed here to prove assertion strength. To keep the removal itself from being a shortcut, the authority runs a one-time surgical review — each changed file equals its base blob plus only the named edits — and a one-time global inventory: a tracked name-set diff union `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, driven red with a planted tracked outside path and a planted nonignored untracked outside path and green clean on a throwaway fixture. Those are plan and authority evidence; **no permanent base-pinned test block is added**. Ignored paths are outside Git inventory, and authorized reports live outside the repository, so no local raw report is tracked or committed and no hostname or private absolute path enters a public artifact. The full CI-equivalent `bun run validate:ci` runs once, at the plan's `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` under `--assertions final --run-commands` before apply/archive; the post-archive verdict evaluates focused retained-suite evidence and never reruns the root suite. The `prepin fixture discovery` test is retitled for its truthful no-test-files invariant, and the `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-1-DE5A1A05 checkout and README guards` describe is retitled for its README-only content.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the declaration-count guard and its full-history checkout. Rejected: the guard counts declarations in existing files, not executed code or assertion strength, and it fails open in a shallow checkout; keeping it would preserve a falsely reassuring green and the depth requirement that serves only it. This is the decision the maintainer asked to overturn, and the counter-argument is answered in the Rationale rather than ignored.

Replace the declaration-count guard with a code-coverage threshold. Rejected: a percentage floor is another volume proxy that a test can satisfy without asserting behavior, it adds a reporter and configuration to a public package, and it is not the policy the repository states. Diagnostic coverage belongs to a future separately ratified change, not to this retirement.

Remove the depth requirement but keep the guard by vendoring the historical test bytes into the repository so no Git object is read. Rejected: it preserves a misleading measure, adds a permanent duplicate of test sources that can drift, and does not answer the guard's inability to detect behavioral loss. The guard and the depth requirement retire together.

Repair the committed `test-metrics.json` by adding a SHA-256 source digest, a versioned schema, and a `group` field, as the earlier draft proposed. Rejected: that is a cache-repair, not a cache-removal; the digest, the provisional tree-derived artifact, the `sourceCount` helper, and the no-write-when-fresh branch all exist only to keep a committed cache consistent, and the cache adds committed churn without protecting anything a fresh raw report does not already provide. The report is generated afresh per invocation, so it is current by construction.

Identify freshness by file mtimes or a timestamp instead of a digest. Rejected: mtimes are checkout-dependent and unstable in CI, and a timestamp cannot detect a content change. This bundle does not need a freshness identity at all.

Assert that recorded JUnit case counts equal source `it(`/`test(` declaration counts. Rejected: they are different populations here — one counts executed test cases, the other counts syntactic tokens — so the assertion would be false or would force a count of the wrong thing. No count is compared.

Keep `validateJobCheckoutDepth` and add a negative guard that the `validate` job has no `fetch-depth`. Rejected: adding a new static guard for a config key would begin rebuilding the test-volume scaffolding this bundle removes; the removal is covered by the plan's `MustNotContain` assertions on the workflow and by the one-time surgical review.

Mandate a test-only runner seam so a fake spawn can prove one-spawn and fresh-output behavior in-process. Rejected: a production file should not grow a test-only seam, and the seam was proposed only to make digest-cache testing cheap. The real runner is driven through the absolute Bun executable with a fake inner `bun` on `PATH`, so the outer process is the production entry and the fake intercepts only the inner suite spawn.

Add a permanent base-pinned inventory or surgical-shape test block to the suite. Rejected: that reintroduces a full-history dependency into the depth-one job that this bundle is retiring, and it turns a one-time closure measurement into a permanent source-shape ratchet. The surgical review and the global inventory are one-time close evidence, not a permanent test; both halves are expressed at archive close in one discriminating command that pairs a `git diff --exit-code` negative pathspec with a `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` capture and an emptiness test.

Commit a sanitized report, or keep a tracked cache of a report, so the bytes are reviewable in the repository. Rejected: raw JUnit contains hostnames and absolute paths, so committing it would publish machine identifiers; sanitizing it would make the committed and uploaded evidence differ from the bytes the runner produced; and a tracked cache reintroduces exactly the committed churn this bundle removes. Reports stay outside the repository and are never committed.

Run the upload step only with `if: success()`, and make its own failures non-fatal with `continue-on-error`. Rejected: `if: success()` skips the evidence exactly when a failing suite makes it most valuable; `continue-on-error` on the upload step cannot erase an earlier `Run CI validation` failure — the two step statuses are independent and the job still fails — but it would make an upload failure nonfatal, so the step runs with `if: always()` and no `continue-on-error`.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Measured executed-code coverage remains diagnostic-only and unimplemented. If the maintainer chooses to measure it, that is a separate, separately ratified change with its own spec and acceptance criteria; this bundle adds no reporter, threshold, or tooling and does not claim the surviving targeted tests replace a coverage floor.

The record-payment question is answered as none. This bundle writes no `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` record entry and flushes no record XML; the overturns are durable in the spec's `Problem`, `Constraints`, and acceptance criteria and here. No byte-invariance criterion is therefore made to permit a record write.

`publish.yml`'s three `fetch-depth: 0` declarations are out of scope and stay; they serve the publish workflow's own contracts, not the retired guard. A future change that needs less history there is its own bundle.

Whether the report should contain only the slowest slice, be truncated, or gain a retention policy is out of scope. This bundle uploads the current report verbatim so the evidence equals what the runner produced; the report lives outside the repository, so no artifact-size or retention question is decided here.

Scenarios.Scenario: The human-ratification stop: the spec is written `status="draft"` and stops there. The implementation authority requests ratification of `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6` at spec stage only after its own review, and only a sufficient phrase from the maintainer moves it to `approved`. No plan, approval gate, execute epoch, apply, or close runs before that phrase.

The fresh-report path: `test:metrics` runs. No `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` is set, so the runner creates a unique directory under `os.tmpdir()`, resolves `junit.xml` inside it, removes any file already there, spawns `bun test` once with `--reporter=junit` writing that file, prints the report path and the slowest ranking parsed from that report, and exits with the child's status. Nothing inside the repository changes.

The override and clear path: `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` names a path outside the repository. The runner creates the parent directory if needed, removes a stale file already at the path, spawns the suite once, and writes the current report there. A stale report from a previous run can never be mistaken for this run's output.

The override refusal path: `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` resolves inside the repository, directly or through a symlinked parent. The runner canonicalizes the path, finds it inside the repository, refuses with a diagnostic nonzero, performs no `mkdir`/unlink/spawn, and leaves a planted file at the lexical target byte-identical; the fake child records zero attempts.

The report-refusal paths: the child succeeds but the current report is missing, unreadable, or malformed, so the runner exits nonzero with a diagnostic, prints no ranking, and reuses no stale report. The Bun spawn fails or yields no usable status, so the runner exits nonzero and does not retry. A fake child exits 7, so the runner preserves exit 7 and retains any report bytes the fake produced.

The suite lifecycle: the full `bun run validate:ci` runs once at the plan's `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` under `--assertions final --run-commands`, before apply/archive. After the archive move the verdict evaluates only the focused retained-suite evidence, so the root suite is never run a second time.

The failure path: the inner suite exits non-zero; the runner propagates a nonzero OS exit and leaves the failure report in place. Restoring the failing assertion makes the next run exit zero and produce a fresh report. The fake inner `bun` records exactly one invocation per run, so the single-spawn property is observed on the real outer entry.

CI on a failing suite: `Run CI validation` fails inside `bun run validate:ci`. Because the upload step uses `if: always()`, it still runs and uploads `${{ runner.temp }}/ngrace-test-reports/junit.xml`; because it sets no `continue-on-error`, its success does not change the job's failure outcome, so the test failure is neither hidden nor replaced.

A tracked outside write, or a first-time nonignored untracked write: a reviewer appends to `CHANGELOG.md` or drops a new nonignored file under another path. The one-time global inventory lists the extra path, it is outside the seven deliverables and this bundle's arrival, and the close reddens. An ignored path is not reported by `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, so it is not claimed by this scenario or any criterion.

A shortcut removal: an executor deletes an unrelated assertion, keeps a retired symbol, or reformats beyond the named edits. The plan's `MustContain`/`MustNotContain` assertions and the one-time surgical review catch it; no permanent base-pinned test is needed.

A post-close applied-archive tree: the declaration-count guard, `validateJobCheckoutDepth`, the JSON import, and the metrics-staleness assertions are absent; the README-only describe is retitled; the `prepin CI retirement` guard and the `prepin fixture discovery` fixture-walker test are present; `fetch-depth: 0` is absent from the `validate` job; `NGRACE_TEST_REPORT_PATH` and the `always()` upload step are present; `test-metrics.json` is absent; the kept runner, parser, and ranking tests and the focused retained-suite evidence pass; the full `validate:ci` ran once before apply/archive and is not rerun; lint is 0/0; and the combined Git inventory contains only the seven deliverables and this bundle's archive arrival.
